text: Found it: `Interval.fromISO` calls `DateTime.fromISO` directly, so with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` an unparsable half (e.g. the duration in `2007-03-01T13:00:00/P1Y2M10DT2H30M`) throws an InvalidDateTimeError before the duration branch is reached. Fix: wrap each `DateTime.fromISO` call in try/catch and treat a throw as "not valid". Applying and verifying now.

#1 fixed and verified: `Interval.fromISO` now wraps both `DateTime.fromISO` calls in try/catch (treating a throw as "not valid"), so with `Settings.throwOnInvalid = true` the duration branches are reached and valid ISO intervals no longer throw. Checked: the three valid forms (start/end, start/duration, duration/end) all return the expected interval, garbage/null/empty/repeat-format/backwards still throw; full suite unchanged (892 pass, only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures). Only src/interval.js was modified.

#2 in progress: the bug is in `objToLocalTS` in src/impl/util.js — its legacy year fix-up does `d.setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`, which keeps the month/day normalized in the 19XX/2000 space. When a day overflow lands on Feb 29 2000 (leap) the year is then forced to 100 (not leap), so the result is off by a day (e.g. 0099-12-31 + 61 days gives 0100-03-01 instead of 0100-03-02). Fix: `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)` so the raw fields are normalized in the target year. Applying and verifying now.

#4 in progress: the bug is in the `isInDST` getter in src/datetime.js — it compares against `this.set({ month: 1 })`, which keeps the current day-of-month, so in 1974 (when the USA was on DST from Jan 6 to Oct 27) the January reference is itself DST and `isInDST` wrongly returns false. Fix: use `this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 })` as the standard-time reference. Applying and verifying now.

#5 in progress: the bug is in `casualMatrix` in src/duration.js — the `quarters` entry is missing the `seconds` conversion (the `accurateMatrix` quarters entry has it), so any quarters<->seconds conversion yields NaN (e.g. `Duration.fromObject({quarters: 1, seconds: 1}).normalize()`). Fix: add `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60` to that entry. Applying and verifying now.

#2 fixed and verified. `objToLocalTS` in src/impl/util.js now does `d.setUTCFullYear(obj.year, obj.month - 1, obj.day)` (with an explanatory comment) instead of `d.setUTCFullYear(d.getUTCFullYear() - 1900)`, so the raw calendar fields are normalized in the target year rather than keeping a month/day normalized in the 19XX/2000 space. Before: `0099-12-31 + 61 days` gave 0100-03-01; after: 0100-03-02 (and +62 days -> 0100-03-03, 0100-01-02 - 2 days -> 0099-12-31). A cross-check of `objToLocalTS` against a 4000-year-shifted reference over a grid of years 0-100 / months / out-of-range days went from 19 mismatches to 0. Full suite unchanged (892 pass, only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures).

#4 fixed and verified. The `isInDST` getter in src/datetime.js now uses `this.set({ month: 1, day: 1 })` (Jan 1 = standard time) instead of `this.set({ month: 1 })`, which kept the current day-of-month and so could itself land in DST. Before: 250 of the 295 days from 1974-01-06 to 1974-10-27 in America/New_York wrongly reported `isInDST === false`; after: 0 (e.g. 1974-01-06 -> true, 1974-06-15 -> true, 1974-10-26 -> true, 1974-10-27 noon -> false, which is correct because 1974 DST ended at 02:00 that day). Normal years, fixed-offset zones and the southern hemisphere still behave correctly, and the full suite is unchanged (892 pass, only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures).
#1 is fixed and verified (src/interval.js: `Interval.fromISO` now try/catches both `DateTime.fromISO` calls so `Settings.throwOnInvalid` no longer breaks the duration branches).
#2 is fixed and verified (src/impl/util.js: `objToLocalTS` now re-sets year+month+day together, fixing day overflow across the year-100 February boundary).
#4 is fixed and verified (src/datetime.js: `isInDST` now compares against `set({ month: 1, day: 1 })`, so 1974-01-06..1974-10-27 in the USA all report true).

#5: fix applied to src/duration.js (added the missing `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60` to `casualMatrix.quarters`); final verification (all-unit-pairs normalize check + full test suite) is still running, ~4 minutes.

#7 in progress: the bug is `padStart` in src/impl/util.js — it pads by slicing the concatenated string, so negative numbers come out as "00-10" instead of "-0010" (e.g. `DateTime.fromObject({year: -10, month: 5, day: 25, zone: "utc"}).toISODate()` gives "00-10-05-25" instead of "-0010-05-25"). Fix: pad the digits and keep the minus sign in front, preserving the existing no-truncation behaviour for non-negative inputs. Applying and verifying now.

#7 fixed and verified. `padStart` in src/impl/util.js now pads the digits and keeps the minus sign in front (without truncating long digit strings). Before: `DateTime.fromObject({year: -10, month: 5, day: 25, zone: "utc"}).toISODate()` gave "0-10-05-25"; after: "-0010-05-25". Direct checks: padStart(-10,4)="-0010", padStart(-21,4)="-0021", padStart(-5,2)="-05", while padStart(1982,2)="1982", padStart(118040,4)="118040", padStart(7,6)="000007" are unchanged, and the existing [±YYYYY] cases (118040 / -118040) still pass. Full suite unchanged (892 pass, only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures).

#8 in progress: the bug is that `FixedOffsetZone.isValid` unconditionally returns `true`, so a zone built with a non-numeric offset (e.g. `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp")` / `FixedOffsetZone.instance("blorp")`) claims to be valid and a DateTime in it is not marked invalid. Fix: return `isNumber(this.fixed)`. Applying and verifying now.

#8 fixed and verified. src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js now imports `isNumber` and its `isValid` getter returns `isNumber(this.fixed)`. Before: `new FixedOffsetZone("blorp").isValid` was true and a DateTime in that zone was invalid only with reason "invalid input"; after: the zone reports `isValid === false` and the DateTime is invalid with reason "unsupported zone". Numeric zones are unaffected (utcInstance/instance(0)/instance(-300) valid, instance(-300).name "UTC-5"), string zones ("UTC+3", "utc-3:30", "blorp") behave as before, the whole zones suite passes (32/32), and the full suite is unchanged (892 pass, only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures).
#1 fixed and verified (src/interval.js).
#2 fixed and verified (src/impl/util.js: objToLocalTS).
#4 fixed and verified (src/datetime.js: isInDST).

#5: the fix is in the working tree (src/duration.js now has `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60` in casualMatrix.quarters), but the verification subagent is still running its full all-unit-pairs check; I'll confirm within ~3 minutes.
#7 fixed and verified (src/impl/util.js: padStart now handles negative numbers).
#8 fixed and verified (src/zones/fixedOffsetZone.js: isValid returns isNumber(this.fixed)).

#5 fixed and verified. src/duration.js now has `seconds: 91 * 24 * 60 * 60` in `casualMatrix.quarters` (the only change in that file). Before: `Duration.fromObject({quarters: 1, seconds: 1}).normalize()` gave `{quarters: NaN, seconds: NaN}` and `.as("seconds")` gave 0; after: `{quarters: 1, seconds: 1}` and 7862401, with `shiftTo("seconds")` giving 7862400 per quarter and `shiftTo("quarters")` giving 1/7862400 per second. The duration suite passes 114/114 and the full suite is unchanged (892 pass, only the 2 pre-existing French-locale toFormat failures).
